\chapter{Complexity — Oracle Agreement}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.OracleAgreement}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Oracle queries within a time bound]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $O$ be an oracle
language over its alphabet, let $x$ be an input word, and let $t$ be a nonnegative
integer. The list of queries made within this bound consists of the query strings in the
configurations reached after $s$ steps, for each integer $s$ with $0\le s<t$ for which
the machine is in its query state.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Step Equality When Query Answers Agree]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_query_agree}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_query_agree}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_ne_qQuery}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O,O'$ be languages over its symbol alphabet,
and let $c$ be a configuration. Suppose that whenever $c$ is in the query state, its
query string belongs to $O$ if and only if it belongs to $O'$. Then one step from $c$
relative to $O$ equals one step from $c$ relative to $O'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Agreement of Runs Under Agreeing Queries]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_eq_of_agree}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_eq_of_agree}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.fixChoice, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_append, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith, Turing.OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.step_eq_of_query_agree}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic oracle Turing machine, let $O$ and $O'$ be languages over
its symbol alphabet, and let $x$ be an input word and $w$ a finite sequence of choice
bits. Suppose that for every $s<|w|$, if the run of $N$ with oracle $O$ on the first $s$
bits of $w$, starting from its initial configuration on $x$, is in the query state, then
its query string belongs to $O$ if and only if it belongs to $O'$. Then for every $s\le
|w|$, the configurations reached using the first $s$ bits of $w$ are equal for the two
oracles.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Replicated Choices Match Deterministic Running]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_replicate}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_replicate}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM, Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM_runWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ be a language over its symbol alphabet, and
let $x$ be an input word. For natural numbers $s,t$ with $s\le t$, running the
nondeterministic oracle machine associated to $M$ with oracle $O$ on the first $s$ bits
of a length-$t$ sequence of false choice bits, from its initial configuration on $x$,
gives the same configuration as running $M$ with oracle $O$ for $s$ steps from its
initial configuration on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Runs agree on encountered queries]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_query_agree}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_query_agree}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_eq_of_agree, Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_replicate, Turing.OracleTM.toOracleNDTM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ and $O'$ be oracle languages, and let $x$
be an input word. Suppose that whenever the run from the initial configuration on $x$
using $O$ is in the query state at some time $s<t$, the query string then submitted has
the same membership status in $O$ and $O'$. Then the configurations reached after $t$
steps using $O$ and $O'$ are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length bound for a filtered query]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.length_le_of_mem_filtered_queries}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.length_le_of_mem_filtered_queries}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ assign a finite word to each natural number, let $p$ be a predicate on the
natural numbers, and let $t$ be a natural number. Suppose that for every $s<t$, the
length of $f(s)$ is at most $s$. Every word $z$ that appears among the words $f(s)$
selected by $p(s)$ for $s<t$ has length at most $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Runs agree on short oracle queries]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_agree_length_lt}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_agree_length_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_query_agree}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ and $O'$ be oracle languages, and let $x$
be an input word. Suppose that for every word $z$ with $|z|<t$, membership in $O$ and
$O'$ agrees. Then the configurations reached after $t$ steps from the initial
configuration on $x$, using $O$ and $O'$ respectively, are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Runs agree on queries made]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_agree_queriesWithin}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_agree_queriesWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_of_query_agree}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ and $O'$ be oracle languages, and let $x$
be an input word. If membership in $O$ and $O'$ agrees for every query string submitted
by $M$ during the first $t$ steps of its run on $x$ with oracle $O$, then the
configurations reached after $t$ steps on $x$ using $O$ and $O'$ are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length bound for queries within a run]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.length_le_of_mem_queriesWithin}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.length_le_of_mem_queriesWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.length_le_of_mem_filtered_queries, Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin, Turing.OracleTM.queryString_length_le}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $O$ be an oracle
language, and let $x$ be an input word. For every natural number $t$, each query
recorded among the queries made during the first $t$ configurations of the run of $M$
with oracle $O$ from its initial configuration on $x$ has length at most $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on the number of queries]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin_length_le}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin_length_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.queriesWithin}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $O$ be an oracle
language, and let $x$ be an input word. For every natural number $t$, the list of
queries made during the first $t$ configurations of the run from the initial
configuration on $x$ has length at most $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Queries along a choice sequence]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.queriesAlong}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.queriesAlong}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleTM.queryString}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let
$O$ be an oracle language over its alphabet, let $x$ be an input word, and let $w$ be a
finite sequence of choice bits. The list of queries consists of the query strings in the
configurations reached from the initial configuration on $x$ after the first $s$
choices, for each $s$ with $0\le s<|w|$ for which the machine is in its query state.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Agreement under short-query oracle agreement]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_eq_of_agree_length_lt}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_eq_of_agree_length_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.queryString_runWith_length_le, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_eq_of_agree}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine, let $O$ and $O'$ be oracle
languages, and let $x$ be an input word and $w$ a finite sequence of choice bits.
Suppose that for every word $z$ with $|z|<|w|$, membership in $O$ agrees with membership
in $O'$. Then running $N$ with either oracle on $w$ from its initial configuration on
$x$ yields the same final configuration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Agreement on queries along a computation]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_eq_of_agree_queriesAlong}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith_eq_of_agree_queriesAlong}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.initCfg, Turing.OracleNDTM.queriesAlong, Turing.OracleNDTM.runWith, Turing.OracleTM.runWith_take_eq_of_agree}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine, let $O$ and $O'$ be oracle
languages, and let $x$ be an input word and $w$ a finite sequence of choice bits.
Suppose that every query word encountered when running $N$ with $O$ from its initial
configuration on $x$ using $w$ has the same membership status in $O$ and $O'$. Then the
final configurations obtained by running $N$ with $O$ and with $O'$ on $w$ from that
initial configuration are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length of a Query Along a Run]
\lean{Turing.OracleNDTM.length_le_of_mem_queriesAlong}
\label{Turing.OracleNDTM.length_le_of_mem_queriesAlong}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OracleNDTM, Turing.OracleNDTM.queriesAlong, Turing.OracleNDTM.queryString_runWith_length_le, Turing.OracleTM.length_le_of_mem_filtered_queries}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be an oracle nondeterministic Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle language, let
$x$ be an input word, and let $w$ be a finite binary choice word. If a word $z$ occurs
among the queries made along the run of $N$ with oracle $O$ on input $x$ under $w$, then
the length of $z$ is at most the length of $w$.
\end{theorem}
